Short answer: a line out hands a signal to another device's input; a headphone out hands a signal to a pair of transducers. A headphone jack is a line out with a small power amplifier and a volume control in front of it. On the the two are separate Audio/Connector/Phone/TRS/3.5mm jacks with independent level controls, so the recorder can feed a camera or an interface at a steady level while headphone volume moves freely.

The distinction is about current, not voltage. Both jacks swing about a volt. A coaxial connector carrying one signal: a center pin for the signal, an outer shell for ground and shield. Every channel needs its own connector, so a stereo pair takes two and component video takes three.
Also called a phono connector, after its first job of wiring a phonograph into a radio receiver, and cinch in France and Germany after the Chicago manufacturer of that name.

Introduced by the Radio Corporation of America by 1937 inside the model U-109 radio-phonograph, and on the rear panels of its radios by 1938. Through the 1950s it displaced the 6.35 mm phone connector across consumer hi-fi.

Typically implemented via the Client Credentials flow (RFC 6749 §4.4)

-F sets the field separator (FS) used to split each input line into fields.
My Note by default the field separator is any whitespace (space or tab chars). awk -F is useful if you need to customize that some more.
<sep> can be a literal character or an ERE (extended regular expression).
Without -F, awk splits on runs of whitespace (spaces and tabs, collapsing consecutive ones).
With -F, each line is split on the given separator; fields are referenced as $1, $2, ... $NF.
The field separator is also available as the built-in variable FS; -F'\t' is equivalent to BEGIN { FS = "\t" }.
